theme: 3 terms on protocols every value type should adopt: comparing for equality, storing in sets and dictionaries, and ordering for sorting

terms.definition: A protocol that lets a type check whether two of its values are equal with `==`.
terms.example: `Point` is Equatable, so I can check `a == b` in the unit test.

terms.definition: A protocol that lets a type be stored in a set or used as a dictionary key.
terms.example: I made `Tag` Hashable, so we can keep tags in a `Set`.

terms.definition: A protocol that lets a type order its values with `<` so they can be sorted.
terms.example: `Level` is Comparable, so `sorted()` works without a closure.

video.title: Equatable, Hashable & Comparable | Day 31
video.description:
Learn to explain how Swift compares, stores and sorts your types: Equatable, Hashable & Comparable, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Equatable - A protocol that lets a type check whether two of its values are equal with `==`.
Hashable - A protocol that lets a type be stored in a set or used as a dictionary key.
Comparable - A protocol that lets a type order its values with `<` so they can be sorted.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Equatable, Hashable & Comparable in English | Day 31
landscape.description:
Explain Equatable, Hashable & Comparable in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
이퀘터블, 해셔블, 컴패러블 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Equatable - A protocol that lets a type check whether two of its values are equal with `==`.
한국어: 이퀘터블: `==`로 두 값이 같은지 비교할 수 있게 해 주는 프로토콜

Hashable - A protocol that lets a type be stored in a set or used as a dictionary key.
한국어: 해셔블: 타입을 Set에 담거나 Dictionary의 키로 쓸 수 있게 해 주는 프로토콜

Comparable - A protocol that lets a type order its values with the less-than operator so they can be sorted.
한국어: 컴패러블: less-than 연산자로 값의 순서를 정해 정렬할 수 있게 해 주는 프로토콜

In this video, Mina and Jake fix a red `Set`, argue whether equal is enough for sorting and add a less-than function, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain these protocol terms in English?

dialogue.title: Why is the set red?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, why is your `Set` red? Did you forget something on `Tag`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, a `Set` needs Hashable, so I added it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. Hashable also needs Equatable, but Swift writes `==` for you here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So Equatable just checks if two tags are the same?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. It compares every property with `==`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then `tags.sorted()` should work too. Equatable is enough, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. Equatable only says same or not. Sorting needs Comparable.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, my mistake. So I add Comparable and write `<`?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. You write one `<` function, and Swift gives you the other comparisons.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. Now `name` decides the order, so a comes before b.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Perfect. Hashable for sets, Comparable for sorting.
Make it Equatable, and `==` can compare two values.
